claims.claim: Victories: Aeschylus 13, Sophocles 18 (some sources 20 or 24), Euripides 4 in his lifetime (a fifth posthumously).
Theatre capacity 6,000 to over 15,000 (estimates); Athenian adult male citizens perhaps 30,000–50,000 in the 5th century.
Thirty-two complete tragedies survive: 7 Aeschylus (Prometheus disputed), 7 Sophocles, 18 or 19 Euripides (Rhesus disputed).
Aeschylus fought at Marathon (490 BC), where his brother Cynegirus died; his epitaph mentions Marathon only; died in Sicily 456 BC.
claims.source: Herodotus 6.114; Life of Aeschylus; Pausanias 1.14.5; Athenaeus 14.627c

claims.claim: Athenaeus 8.347e: Aeschylus called his tragedies 'slices from the great banquets of Homer'.
Herodotus I.207: Croesus says his sufferings have been his lessons.
Robert F. Kennedy, Indianapolis, 4 April 1968, quoted Agamemnon in Edith Hamilton's translation ('the awful grace of God'); the city stayed largely calm.
claims.source: Text of the speech (JFK Library); Edith Hamilton, The Greek Way (1930)

claims.claim: Ephialtes' reforms 462/461 BC; Ephialtes assassinated soon after.

claims.claim: A tie vote acquits ('the vote of Athena') became Athenian practice.
Froma Zeitlin, 'The Dynamics of Misogyny', Arethusa 11 (1978); E. R. Dodds, 'Morals and Politics in the Oresteia' (1960).
Sophocles born Colonus c. 496 BC; general 441/440 with Pericles; over 120 plays; OT probably 420s; OC staged posthumously 401 BC.
claims.source: Life of Sophocles; Plutarch, Pericles 8; Androtion fr.; standard

claims.claim: Plague at Athens 430–426 BC; Pericles died 429 BC.
Aristotle thought Oedipus the model tragedy (Poetics XIII, XIV and passim).
E. R. Dodds, 'On Misunderstanding the Oedipus Rex', Greece & Rome 13 (1966); Bernard Knox, Oedipus at Thebes (1957); Vernant, 'Ambiguity and Reversal' (1970).
Freud, The Interpretation of Dreams (1899, dated 1900), ch. V, on Oedipus.

Antigone 672: anarchy the worst of evils.

Hegel on Antigone: Phenomenology (1807); Lectures on Aesthetics ('one of the most sublime ... works of art').
claims.source: Hegel, Aesthetics, tr. Knox (1975) II, p. 1218

Simone Weil, 'Antigone' (1936) for Entre nous, the factory bulletin at Rosières; in Intimations of Christianity among the Ancient Greeks (1957).

A page is lost after Bacchae 1329; Christus Patiens preserves lines used to reconstruct Agave's lament; Christus Patiens attributed to Gregory of Nazianzus, date and author uncertain.

Steiner, The Death of Tragedy (1961); Sayers, 'The Greatest Drama Ever Staged' (1938); MacKinnon; Rowan Williams, The Tragic Imagination (2016).
